description: A global search feature that allows users to instantly search across articles, pages, and other content on the website.
target_audience: Website visitors looking for specific information, case studies, or services.
goals: Provide a fast, intuitive way to navigate the site's content.
Reduce bounce rates by helping users find relevant articles and pages quickly.
Ensure the search experience is accessible and keyboard-friendly.

requirements.title: Search Interface
requirements.description: A search input accessible via the global Navbar and a standard keyboard shortcut (e.g., Cmd/Ctrl + K) to open a search modal.

requirements.title: Instant Results (As-you-type)
requirements.description: Search results should populate dynamically as the user types, with a slight debounce to optimize performance.

requirements.title: Categorized Results
requirements.description: Search results must be organized by categories: 'Articles', 'Pages', and 'Content/Services' for easier scanning.

requirements.title: Keyboard Navigation
requirements.description: Users must be able to navigate through search results using the Up/Down arrow keys and hit Enter to visit a result.

requirements.title: Empty State & 'No Results'
requirements.description: Display a helpful empty state before typing, and a clear 'No results found' message with suggested links if a query returns nothing.

requirements.title: Accessibility (a11y)
requirements.description: The search modal must trap focus, use appropriate ARIA labels, and announce results to screen readers.

technical_specifications.frontend: React Client Component using standard HTML inputs. Animations for the modal handled by GSAP/Framer Motion. Icons via Lucide React.
technical_specifications.data_source: Next.js API route (e.g., `/api/search`) that aggregates and indexes local static content, or a local index file parsed by Fuse.js for client-side fuzzy searching.
technical_specifications.state_management: Local component state for the query and a global context or Zustand/Jotai for the modal open/close state.

success_metrics: Search usage rate: Percentage of sessions that use the search feature.
Click-through rate: Percentage of searches that result in a click.
Zero-result rate: Percentage of queries returning no results (to inform future content needs).
